questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical cross-region disaster recovery knowledge with real AWS services and automation capabilities. Evaluates understanding of RTO/RPO constraints, service integration, and operational readiness.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-region RDS read replicas with automated promotion
- S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with Replication Time Control
- Route 53 health checks and failover routing policies
- Cross-account IAM trust relationships and role-based access
- CloudWatch alarm-driven automation via EventBridge/Step Functions

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: DR Stack - Cross-Region Failover Resources
Resources:
  DRRDSReadReplica:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties:
      SourceDBInstanceIdentifier: !Sub 'arn:aws:rds:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:db:prod-primary'
      DBInstanceClass: db.t3.medium
      AvailabilityZone: us-west-2a
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: dr

  DRDataLakeBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub 'datalake-dr-${AWS::AccountId}'
      ReplicationConfiguration:
        Role: !GetAtt ReplicationRole.Arn
        Rules:
          - Destination:
              Bucket: !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:::datalake-dr'
              StorageClass: STANDARD
            ID: CRR-Rule
            Status: Enabled
            SourceSelectionCriteria:
              Ssecs:
                SseAwsKmsKeyId: !Ref DataLakeKey

  ReplicationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: s3.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole

  Route53FailoverRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      Name: api.example.com
      Type: A
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      SetIdentifier: primary
      Failover:
        Type: PRIMARY
      HealthCheckId: !Ref PrimaryHealthCheck
      AliasTarget:
        DNSName: !GetAtt PrimaryALB.DNSName
        HostedZoneId: !GetAtt PrimaryALB.CanonicalHostedZoneID

  Route53DRRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      Name: api.example.com
      Type: A
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      SetIdentifier: dr
      Failover:
        Type: SECONDARY
      AliasTarget:
        DNSName: !GetAtt DRALB.DNSName
        HostedZoneId: !GetAtt DRALB.CanonicalHostedZoneID

  PrimaryHealthCheck:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck
    Properties:
      HealthCheckConfig:
        Type: HTTPS
        FullyQualifiedDomainName: api.example.com
        Port: 443
        ResourcePath: /health
        RequestInterval: 30
        FailureThreshold: 3
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question probes practical, beginner-friendly incident response design that minimizes MTTR in a single-region deployment.

## Key Concepts
- Route 53 health checks and failover routing
- CloudFront serving a maintenance page from S3
- ECS Fargate autoscaling and safe-state handling
- Rollback plan and verification

## Code Example
```hcl
# Route53 health check and failover (simplified)
resource "aws_route53_health_check" "web" {
  fqdn = "app.example.com"
  type = "HTTPS"
  request_interval = 30
  failure_threshold = 3
}
```
```hcl
# Route53 record with primary/secondary failover (simplified)
resource "aws_route53_record" "primary" {
  name    = "app.example.com"
  type    = "A"
  zone_id = var.zone_id
  alias {
    name                   = aws_lb.app.dns_name
    zone_id                = aws_lb.app.zone_id
    evaluate_target_health = true
  }
  set_identifier = "primary"
  failover_routing_policy { type = "PRIMARY" }
  health_check_id = aws_route53_health_check.web.id
}
```
```json
# CloudFront config would point to a maintenance S3 bucket when the primary is unavailable
```

- What metrics and alarms would you add to ensure quick detection and safe rollback?
